nonvacuity: An explicit family, rather than an implication with assumed premises. For r=2 (N=4), the 16 assignments have strictly positive product weights and total 1. Exact enumeration gives V=E(Vhat)=7/4, P(all pairs split)=49/64, and Var(N Vhat)=81/14. The same construction exists for every r>=2; outcomes of existing units are fixed. See scratch/exact-checks.json.

For every N=n+1 use independent fair binary exposures and y(i,0)=y(i,1)=1, with the same table across sizes. Reindex its 2^N assignments by Fin(2^N) to obtain an ExperimentSequence. Both marginals are 1/2, ComparisonBounded holds with c1=1,c2=2, and the diagonal graph gives genuine C5 with m=1. The effect estimate is (2/N)sum_i(2Z_i-1), tau=0, V=4/N, and Vhat=4/N at every assignment. Thus C6 holds with c=4, the lower-tail probabilities and Var(N Vhat) are zero, and b=1/4 works for both joint-rate clauses. The positive-joint domain is empty only at N=1 in this instance.

The displayed four atoms have weights 2/9,4/9,1/9,2/9 and all marginals strictly between 0 and 1. Lean checks compile the marginals, total, expectation 2/9 for outcomes (2,-1), and expectation -1/3 for outcomes (1,-1). The actual and simulated draws are independent on a 16-point product space. See scratch/Check.lean.

Use signedReplicationPopulation 2, exposure 1, N=2, R=1, p0=1/3: T=1 and kappa=3. This realizes the signed nonzero-total branch. Replacing the exposure-1 outcomes by (2,1) gives the common-sign branch with kappa=1; replacing them by (1,-1) realizes T=0 in the absolute-bias clause. The fixed positive weights and denominators are unaffected by these outcome changes.

The shared fair Bernoulli experiment has two positive-weight atoms at every N>=1. Take all outcomes zero, treated=1 and control=0. Then StandingPositivity and C3 hold with c1=0,c2=2, and the identity h gives printed C5 with m=1. Every pair has joint 1/2 rather than product 1/4, so any valid g has N^2 true entries and C4 fails. The triangle assertion has nonempty instances already at q=1.

Independent fair binary exposures on N>=1 units, with arbitrary fixed outcomes, have genuine vector dependency for the diagonal h and RowBound(h,1). Distinct units are independent, and g_h is the diagonal matrix with total count N. Thus directed corrected C5 and C4 are simultaneously realized. The graph and no-edge equivalences also have ordinary finite examples without any probability assumptions.

The explicit independent fair-exposure family exists for every N>=1 and uses a fixed infinite outcome table. Its first four units have both outcomes equal to 1; consequently Vhat>0 at every assignment and size. At N=8, exact enumeration gives b=4, tau=0, NV=4, E(N Vhat)=6 and Var(N Vhat)=4. Odd and even block endpoints yield the two distinct limits; no undefined ratio is used.

Take N independent fair Bernoulli exposures, estimate=(2/N)sum_i(2Z_i-1), target=0, and V=Vhat=4/N. Then c=s=4, W=4 identically, E(W)=v=4, Var(W)=0, and Vhat>0 everywhere. The Rademacher central limit theorem gives the required standard normal limit. This realizes even the final, more restrictive implication, rather than merely the coverage clauses.

The same independent fair binary sequence with y(i,0)=y(i,1)=1 has one common outcome table, StandingPositivity, C3 with c1=1,c2=2, and diagonal g satisfying C4 because its density is 1/N. Its treated HT mean has target 1 and variance 1/N. The separate algebraic implication is realized, for example, by estimate=1,target=0,V=1,Vhat=4.

All individual rounding bins are nonempty (their displayed centers lie in them). The theorem asserts that the bins cannot jointly satisfy the midpoint identity; no inconsistent conjunction is used as a premise to prove an unrelated fact. Both possible-center intervals are separated from the corresponding possible-midpoint interval by exactly 1/1000, also checked in Lean.

Lean constructs U=range 100, neighbors=Icc 1 39, i=0,n=10, satisfying every structural, sample-size and sampling-fraction hypothesis. To realize the small-p branch as well, use U=range 80 and n=8 with the same neighbors: p=204/317185<=27/40000 and q=153/57670<1/100. To realize q>=1/100, take |U|=400,n=40, giving q approximately 0.01171. The endpoint n=|U|-39 is also valid and gives q=0.

The two-unit signed model with exposure-1 outcomes (2,-1), R=1, p0=1/3, and b=1/2 has total 1, relative bias 7/9, printed bound 4/9, and satisfies 1>=log(1/2)/log(2/3)-1. Both universal assertions therefore fail on a nonempty, positive-marginal, nonzero-total domain. The witness uses R=1, so permitting R=0 in the negated universals plays no role.

The signed four-atom experiment realizes N=2 and two distinct positive exposures, with signed outcomes and nontrivial total/effect variances. The exclusive two-atom population in scratch/Check.lean has all marginals 1/2, zero distinct-unit same-label joint, and total variance 4. Six additional nonuniform eight-atom signed-outcome examples satisfy every displayed identity by exact enumeration.

Both joint regimes occur. Shared fair exposure on two units has every same-label joint equal to 1/2>0 (compiled). For an exclusive two-unit exposure design with outcomes 1,-1, marginals are 1/2 and the off-diagonal same-label joint is zero (compiled). Exact enumeration gives true total variance 4, E(Q)=2, A=-2 and E(A2)=2, hence E(Q+A2)=4. The bias equality and correction have substantive nonzero values.
